headline: DOLLAR SINKS, GOLD HOLDS $4,600 — Metal Extends Gains as Japan Intervenes in Currency Markets
snippet: Gold steadied at $4,621/oz on May 4 as the US dollar fell sharply following reports of Japanese currency market intervention, with the metal building on a near-2% gain from the prior session. Geopolitical uncertainty from the Middle East conflict and persistent central bank accumulation continue to underpin prices well above $4,500.

headline: CHINA CUTS OFF ACID — Export Ban Takes Effect in May, Putting 15% of Chilean Copper Output at Risk
snippet: China's ban on sulphuric acid exports — triggered by war disruptions to global sulphur supply from the Middle East — took effect this month, threatening Chile's copper sector which imports over one million tonnes of Chinese acid annually for heap-leach refining operations. Acid prices in China have roughly doubled since the conflict began, and analysts warn constrained output from the world's largest copper producer could tighten the already-strained global copper market.

headline: BANK OF AMERICA STANDS FIRM: $6,000 GOLD Target Intact — Silver to Average $86/oz This Year
snippet: Bank of America analysts reiterated their 12-month $6,000/oz gold price target on May 1, citing persistent US dollar weakness and surging central bank demand, while forecasting silver will average $86/oz for 2026 — more than double year-ago levels as industrial and investment demand converge.

headline: GLENCORE + FALCON COPPER SIGN MoU — Up to 1.6M Tonnes/Year in US Critical Minerals Supply Deal
snippet: Falcon Copper Corp. and Glencore International signed a non-binding MoU on April 30 to collaborate on projects supplying copper and critical minerals into the United States, with Glencore expected to provide up to 1.6 million tonnes of copper concentrate annually to Falcon's planned US smelting and refining platform.

headline: RECORD MARGINS — Endeavour Mining Posts $613M Free Cash Flow in Q1 as $4,810 Gold Drives 65% Earnings Jump
snippet: West Africa's largest gold producer posted Q1-2026 free cash flow of $613 million and adjusted EBITDA of $880 million as a realized gold price of $4,810/oz — up 73% year-on-year — more than offset a 17% production decline, with the company's shares jumping 7% on release of the April 30 result.

headline: 1,392 g/t SILVER OVER 1.9 METRES — Americas Gold Hits 4th Major New Vein System at Idaho's Galena Mine
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver (TSX: USA) reported April 30 that drilling from the 4300 Level of Idaho's Galena Mine intercepted six new high-grade silver-copper-antimony veins, highlighted by 1,392 g/t Ag, 1.5% Cu, and 1.5% Sb over 1.9m — the company's fourth major new discovery in just one year of systematic drilling.

headline: COT REPORT: BIG SPECS TRIM GOLD LONGS — Silver Drops 7% in Positioning Reset Before Next Leg
snippet: The May 1 Commitments of Traders report shows large speculators reducing net long positions in both gold and silver, with silver recording a 7.3% weekly decline — a technical reset that analysts interpret as a healthier base for the next move higher rather than a structural trend reversal.

headline: LITHIUM REVIVAL — Core Lithium Starts Ore Mining at Finniss This Month After A$300M Glencore-Backed Restart
snippet: Core Lithium (ASX: CXO) began ore extraction at its Finniss lithium mine in the Northern Territory this month following a fully funded A$300M+ restart package that includes a Glencore offtake agreement and an A$50M surface mining contract awarded to NRW Holdings, with first spodumene concentrate shipments targeted for Q4 2026.

headline: CHINA'S QUIET TIGHTENING — Rare Earth Export Controls Deepen as US Races to Fund Western Supply
snippet: China continued tightening rare earth export controls through late April while US and allied producers rushed to secure alternative supply, with the week of April 27–May 1 seeing fresh capital raises, strategic acquisitions across the Americas, and accelerating consolidation — covered in the Rare Earth Exchanges weekly roundup.

headline: MINING M&A SURGES TO $21.6B — Strongest Q1 Deal Activity Since 2023 as Gold Prices Reactivate Balance Sheets
snippet: Global mining deal volume reached $21.6 billion across 121 transactions in Q1-2026 — the highest first-quarter total since 2023 — as near-record gold prices and energy-transition demand for critical minerals pushed acquirers to act, with precious metals and critical mineral assets in stable jurisdictions drawing the most interest.

headline: URANIUM-COPPER GRADES CONFIRMED — Mustang Energy Hits 15.9% Cu at Saskatchewan's Surprise Creek
snippet: Mustang Energy Corp. (OTC: MECPF) returned bonanza copper-uranium grades from 11 drill holes at the Surprise Creek project northwest of the Athabasca Basin, with hole BOB25-002 hitting 4.9m of 2.69% Cu from surface including a 0.5m interval of 15.9% Cu in a district with known uranium-copper vein mineralisation.

headline: GOLD MINERS STILL CHEAP — Haywood Securities Flags Undervaluation vs. Metal as 'Structural Bull Market' Deepens
snippet: Despite gold trading above $4,600/oz, gold mining equities remain undervalued relative to the metal, Haywood Securities analysts argue — with senior producers trading at just 9.6x forward cash flow versus a five-year average of 8.35x, and the firm's 2026 gold forecast of $4,906/oz suggesting margins have further to expand.
